result.builder:
Goal: add a --tsv flag to the CLI so tab-separated stdin is parsed with a tab separator, while behaviour without the flag stays exactly as it is now. Make one pull request.

Context (current repo state):
- bin/csv2json.js reads stdin with readFileSync(0, 'utf8'), calls parse(text) with no separator, writes JSON.stringify(result) plus '
', and ignores process.argv.
- src/parse.js exports parse(text, sep = ','), which already splits each line on sep. Rows are split on /?
/.
- test/csv.test.js uses node:test and has a 'cli' test that runs bin/csv2json.js through execFileSync with `input`.
- package.json has "test": "node --test".
- README.md shows only `node bin/csv2json.js < table.csv`.

Steps:
1. In bin/csv2json.js, check whether '--tsv' appears anywhere in process.argv.slice(2). If it does, call parse(text, '	'); if not, call parse(text) exactly as today. Leave the output format alone (JSON.stringify with no indentation, then one '
'). Don't change how unknown arguments are handled, and don't add --help, --sep or auto-detection.
2. Leave src/parse.js as it is unless you really need to change it. Fields are still split naively, with no quoting rules.
3. Add tests to test/csv.test.js (or a new test/*.test.js file) using node:test and execFileSync('node', ['bin/csv2json.js', '--tsv'], { input, encoding: 'utf8' }). Each test asserts exact output:
   - input 'a	b
1	2
' -> '[{"a":"1","b":"2"}]
'
   - input 'name	note
x	hello, world
' -> '[{"name":"x","note":"hello, world"}]
'
   - input 'a	b
1	2
3	4
' -> '[{"a":"1","b":"2"},{"a":"3","b":"4"}]
'
   Also add a no-flag test: input 'a	b
1	2
' -> '[{"a\tb":"1\t2"}]
' (the JSON text contains backslash-t escapes). Keep the existing CSV tests.
4. Update README.md: add a section that documents the --tsv flag, shows the example `node bin/csv2json.js --tsv < table.tsv`, and says the flag means the input is tab-separated (fields split on a tab). Keep the existing CSV example.
5. Check from the repo root before you open the PR:
   - printf 'a	b
1	2
' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv; echo "exit=$?"  -> [{"a":"1","b":"2"}] then exit=0
   - printf 'name	note
x	hello, world
' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv  -> [{"name":"x","note":"hello, world"}]
   - printf 'a	b
1	2
3	4
' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv  -> [{"a":"1","b":"2"},{"a":"3","b":"4"}]
   - printf 'a,b
1,2
' | node bin/csv2json.js  -> [{"a":"1","b":"2"}]
   - printf 'a	b
1	2
' | node bin/csv2json.js  -> [{"a	b":"1	2"}]
   - npm test  -> exits 0
6. Commit and open one pull request that describes the change.
result.verifier:
Run every check from the repository root at the pull request's head. Each command stands alone; no shell variables carry over between commands. Run npm install first only if package.json declares dependencies.

Check 1. Expect line: "`printf 'a\tb\n1\t2\n' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv` prints exactly `[{"a":"1","b":"2"}]` followed by a newline and exits 0."
Run: printf 'a\tb\n1\t2\n' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv > /tmp/c1.out; echo "exit=$?"; od -c /tmp/c1.out
Then run: printf '[{"a":"1","b":"2"}]\n' | cmp - /tmp/c1.out && echo SAME
PASS: exit=0 is printed and cmp prints SAME (stdout is exactly [{"a":"1","b":"2"}] plus one newline). FAIL: a different exit status, or stdout differs in any byte.

Check 2. Expect line: "With --tsv, commas inside a field stay literal: `printf 'name\tnote\nx\thello, world\n' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv` prints exactly `[{"name":"x","note":"hello, world"}]` followed by a newline."
Run: printf 'name\tnote\nx\thello, world\n' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv | cmp - <(printf '[{"name":"x","note":"hello, world"}]\n') && echo SAME
PASS: SAME is printed. FAIL: cmp reports a difference, or nothing is printed.

Check 3. Expect line: "With --tsv and several data rows, every row comes out in order: `printf 'a\tb\n1\t2\n3\t4\n' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv` prints exactly `[{"a":"1","b":"2"},{"a":"3","b":"4"}]` followed by a newline."
Run: printf 'a\tb\n1\t2\n3\t4\n' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv | cmp - <(printf '[{"a":"1","b":"2"},{"a":"3","b":"4"}]\n') && echo SAME
PASS: SAME is printed. FAIL: any difference.

Check 4. Expect line: "Without the flag, CSV still works as before: `printf 'a,b\n1,2\n' | node bin/csv2json.js` prints exactly `[{"a":"1","b":"2"}]` followed by a newline."
Run: printf 'a,b\n1,2\n' | node bin/csv2json.js | cmp - <(printf '[{"a":"1","b":"2"}]\n') && echo SAME
PASS: SAME is printed. FAIL: any difference.

Check 5. Expect line: "Without the flag, tabs are not treated as separators: `printf 'a\tb\n1\t2\n' | node bin/csv2json.js` prints exactly `[{"a\tb":"1\t2"}]` followed by a newline, which is the current output."
The expected output is JSON text in which each \t is the two characters backslash and t.
Run: printf 'a\tb\n1\t2\n' | node bin/csv2json.js | cmp - <(printf '[{"a\\tb":"1\\t2"}]\n') && echo SAME
Also run: printf 'a\tb\n1\t2\n' | node bin/csv2json.js | od -c
PASS: SAME is printed (od shows the literal sequence \ t inside the key and the value, and one trailing \n). FAIL: any difference, for example the output being split into keys a and b.

Check 6. Expect line: "`npm test` exits 0, and test/ contains at least one test that runs bin/csv2json.js with --tsv on tab-separated input and checks its output."
Run: npm test; echo "exit=$?"
Then run: grep -n -- '--tsv' test/*.js
Read each matching test.
PASS: exit=0, and at least one test in test/ runs bin/csv2json.js with the --tsv argument, gives it input that contains tab characters, and asserts on what it outputs. FAIL: npm test exits non-zero, or no test in test/ does all three (runs bin/csv2json.js, passes --tsv, gives tab-separated input) and checks the output.

Check 7. Expect line: "README.md documents the --tsv flag with an example invocation."
Read README.md at the head.
PASS: README.md mentions the --tsv flag and shows an example command line that uses --tsv (for example node bin/csv2json.js --tsv < table.tsv). FAIL: --tsv is not mentioned, or there is no example invocation that uses it.

Advisory (not part of PASS/FAIL):
- The issue's proof for check 6 says `npm run test:cli`, but package.json has no test:cli script. Check 6 follows the line's own words and runs `npm test`. If the PR adds a test:cli script, you can also run it and report the result.
- It is good if README.md says that --tsv means tab-separated input.
- You may also check that `printf 'a\tb\n1\t2\n' | node bin/csv2json.js extra --tsv` gives the same output as check 1, since the flag may appear anywhere among the arguments.
